mechanism_references.rc_78: .github/scripts/run-ox-with-retry.sh work-quantum monitor: LEX_WORK_QUANTUM_EXPIRED (seconds=2700). Factory-wide requirements 10 and 12 record that rc-78 is an orchestration guard, not a product, evidence or human-gate problem.
mechanism_references.rc_67: .github/scripts/run-ox-with-retry.sh: when LEX_REQUIRE_DELTA is set (the evaluation lane always sets it in the current core-lane.yml) and the producer session ends with HEAD unchanged and empty git status --porcelain, the wrapper exits 67 LEX_ZERO_DELTA_REPAIR, meaning 'THE PRODUCER FOUND NOTHING TO DO', never 'the lane is broken'.
mechanism_references.dispatch_resilience: core-lane.yml resilience job: when the team job fails and a snapshot branch exists, it dispatches core-lane.yml with resume_from_run_id=<failed run>. This is what produced the five-resume chain above.
mechanism_references.no_gate_no_promotion: core-lane.yml audit runs only if needs.team.result == success; a team job failure therefore means the committed repair work sits unaudited on the team snapshot until a healthy producer run carries it to audit.

recurring_anti_pattern_observed.pattern: 3 of the 6 failed producers (40029231841, 40033424089, 40034534808) ended their only session on a tool call that requested external_directory permission under /home/runner/work/_temp (the workflow git-credentials temp area) - almost certainly probing for a GitHub token - which the permission system auto-rejects. The agent then ended its turn instead of proceeding with lane work, and the zero-delta guard killed the run.
recurring_anti_pattern_observed.rule_for_future_producers: lane producers never need a GitHub token; git push/gh workflow are handled by the workflow steps outside the agent. Probing /home/runner/work/_temp for tokens is out of scope, auto-rejected and wastes the entire session. Start with repo work directly (read state, verify artifacts, write records, commit).
recurring_anti_pattern_observed.scope_note: .github/** is control-plane scope and is NOT edited by this lane; this entry is a recorded observation, not a patch.
